items.rule: 45 CFR 164.510(b)(1)-(3): capable patient opportunity to object; absent-patient pickup by professional judgment; incapacitated best-interest limited relevance.
items.topic: HIPAA family disclosures: express objection, absent patient and incapacitated patient

option_verdicts.basis: Express objection by capable patient blocks discretionary disclosure to helper under 164.510(b).
Professional judgment can allow absent patient's friend to collect designated prescription without prefiled HIPAA authorization.
Incapacitated patient's caregiver may get only directly relevant PHI when in patient's best interest.
Spouse relationship does not automatically confer entire unrelated history over objection.

items.rule: 21 CFR 7.3(m), 7.40–7.42: Class I defined by reasonable probability of serious harms/death, not need for already-confirmed injury or public FDA classification.
items.topic: FDA Class I recall risk determination before formal FDA classification

option_verdicts.basis: Class III requires little adverse health effect risk, not serious harm; do not await classification.
Manufacturer may initiate voluntary recall prior to FDA formal class assessment.
Serious-health-probability hazard meets Class I definition; isolate lot and follow recall steps promptly.
Voluntary recalls are not always Class II and dispensing should not continue pending publication.

items.topic: Community pharmacy CDTM patient-age limitation despite parent consent

option_verdicts.basis: Parent consent cannot eliminate the expressly stated age minimum in community CDTM.
A 17-year-old cannot be treated through this community-CDTM prescribing arrangement.
Schedule VI limitation does not override patient-age restriction.
Alternative Schedule IV action also does not eliminate patient eligibility limit.

items.topic: DSCSA authorized trading partners and six-year product tracing record responsibility

Purchase from ATP and keep required transaction/tracing evidence at least six years.
Written third-party records arrangement is allowed but dispenser retains legal accountability.
Outsourcing record storage does not transfer statutory DSCSA responsibility to vendor.

items.topic: USP <800> antineoplastic automation and pneumatic-tube transport restrictions

option_verdicts.basis: Table1 antineoplastic tablet/capsule cannot use automated counting machinery prone to breakage/dust.
HD liquid prohibited from pneumatic tube even if child-resistant closure.
Non-Table1 HD automated counting may be permitted by documented assessment and facility SOPs.
Mechanical carts or conveyors are not categorically disallowed for all final dosage HDs.

items.topic: Community pharmacy nonsterile compounding service: permissible refusal versus routine business preference

option_verdicts.basis: Business preference/price alone is not listed exemption to customary-compounding obligation.
Professional standards ordinarily require customary simple/moderate nonsterile preparation availability.
This rule does not compel unsafe hazardous Category3 sterile compounding beyond capability.
Documented extenuating circumstance or Board waiver can relieve specified nonsterile duty.

items.topic: Massachusetts multi-drug single-dose packs: sixty-day cap, Schedule exclusions, same-patient repackaging

option_verdicts.basis: Permitted compatible CIV/CVI oral units can be grouped in compliant daily multidrug pack.
Schedule II stimulant cannot be included; refills assertion does not cure.
Up-to-60-day BUD for multidrug unit makes 90-day pack prohibited regardless of stock expiry.
Returned pack can be altered and re-dispensed to same original patient with records and updated label.

items.topic: FDA Medication Guides: inpatient professional administration and home self-administration distinction

option_verdicts.basis: FDA does not demand Guide per every nurse inpatient dose categorically under current enforcement approach.
Guide commonly required when dispensed for patient self-administration at home; inpatient professional administration distinct.
A prior inpatient dose does not waive post-discharge outpatient dispensing guide.
Drug-specific REMS can impose independent Guide obligation despite ordinary inpatient discretion.

items.topic: Pharmacy referral kickbacks and pharmacy-branded blank prescription forms

option_verdicts.basis: Paying nursing-facility employee for steering drug business is prohibited regardless of theoretical patient choice.
Relabeling a kickback as consulting fee does not change its referral purpose.
Blank scripts preprinted with identifying pharmacy referral are prohibited even unsigned.
Prohibition covers giving practitioners blank forms referring to a particular pharmacy.

items.topic: USP <800> and <797> placement: Category 1 hazardous CSP in a C-SCA versus Category 2

option_verdicts.basis: ISO5 C-PEC alone in C-SCA does not authorize Category2/3 routine compounding.
C-SCA permits Category1 HD CSP whether sterile-to-sterile or nonsterile-to-sterile when all standards fulfilled.
Category2 sterile HD compounding requires proper cleanroom suite and containment.
Current USP <797> uses Category1/2/3, not the obsolete low/medium primary classifications.

items.topic: OTC naloxone versus prescription-labeled naloxone under statewide standing order for a third party

option_verdicts.basis: Approved OTC-labelled nasal product can be sold without individual prescription; DCP controlled prescribing rules do not govern that OTC sale.
OTC status depends on presentation and labeling, not active ingredient alone.
Rx-labelled naloxone may be dispensed under MA statewide standing order to third-party helper.

items.topic: USP <800> chemotherapy spill in patient-care area: trained response, readily available spill kit and hazardous waste

Routine nursing work should not continue through contaminated site before decontamination.
Dispose contaminated absorbents/PPE in appropriate regulated HD waste and document exposure.
Sink disposal violates HD spill cleanup/waste precautions; liquid dissolution does not neutralize drug.

items.rule: 105 CMR 720.020/.050/.200 and MGL112 §12D: less expensive FDA Orange Book A-rated same strength/form is interchangeable absent no-substitution, not different release or dose.
items.topic: Massachusetts nonemergency drug interchange: same active ingredient but strength and dosage form must match

option_verdicts.basis: Cheaper A-rated ER 100mg tablet same formulation qualifies, subject to MLID exception list not specified.
Same 100mg IR tablet is not pharmaceutically equivalent to ER tablet due to release form.
Two 50mg tablets are not automatically a same-strength interchangeable 100mg product.
Seek valid prescriber clarification for changed strength or formulation; cannot silently call it generic substitution.

items.rule: USP <797> §4.1/14.3 and official FAQ: ISO5 PEC + ISO7 buffer/ISO8 ante supports Category2; no-test sterile-start Category2 BUD four days room / ten days refrigerated.
items.topic: USP <797> Category 2 nonhazardous sterile IV bag: ISO-classified suite versus SCA and tested BUD limits

option_verdicts.basis: Proper classified ISO7/8 suite with ISO5 PEC supports Category2 sterile compounding.
Unclassified SCA cannot deliver Category2 BUD simply with ISO5 PEC.
Aseptic sterile starting components without sterility test allow up to 4d room or 10d refrigerated when chemically stable.
Short BUD Category2 can be assigned without universal sterility test; some longer BUDs require it.
